notes: On 1 February 2025, in the afternoon, thousands of supporters of the 'Stop the Isolation' movement marched from Waterloo Station to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) in support of far-right activist Tommy Robinson, who was serving an 18-month prison sentence at the time of reporting. The march, during which participants carried banners with slogans such as 'Free Tommy Robinson' and 'Stop the Boats,' crossed Westminster Bridge and concluded at Whitehall. At the call of SUTR, over 5,000 anti-fascist campaigners and trade unionists from Unison, NEU, UCU, PCS, CWU, and Unite organized a counter-demonstration, marching from Piccadilly to Whitehall in London - Westminster (England) and counter-demonstrators highlighting concerns about the rise of far-right movements both in the UK and globally. Police arrested six people from both sides for incidents such as setting off flares, breaching police lines, and spitting on an officer.

On 1 February 2025, members of ACORN Brighton staged a protest outside Hanover Homes in Brighton (England) to oppose the eviction of 80-year-old Trina Bradbury, who was issued a Section 21 notice after her tenancy ended. Protesters carried banners, signs, and leaflets, criticizing the eviction practice and advocating for renters' rights.

On 1 February 2025, at the call of the Save the Sovereign Centre campaign, a large crowd gathered outside the Sovereign Centre in Eastbourne (England) to protest the partial closure of its pools. The demonstration followed Eastbourne Borough Council's decision in November 2024 to shut down two pools due to financial difficulties. While GLL (Better) planned to reopen the shallow pool year-round at the time of reporting, protesters demanded that the fun pool also remain open throughout the year, emphasizing its importance for fitness, accessibility, and therapy for children with disabilities.

On 1 February 2025, around 15 Argentinians living in the UK held a demonstration around the Piccadilly area in London - Westminster (England) against the far-right and to protest the libertarian policies of Argentine President Javier Milei, particularly his criticism of gender ideology and gay couples. The demonstration coincided with the call for a large march in Argentina by the LGTBQ+ community against Milei.

On 1 February 2025, members of Serbian diaspora living in the UK gathered outside the Serbian Embassy in London - Kensington and Chelsea (England) to show solidarity with the student-led protests in Serbia. Protesters carried banners that read 'Corruption killed 15', 'The students from London are with you', and 'Support is coming'. The event was part of a larger anti-corruption protest movement led by students in Serbia and the Serbian diaspora abroad triggered by a deadly canopy collapse at the Novi Sad train station on 1 November 2024.

On 31 January 2025, protesters camped next to a 180-year-old oak tree in Otley (England) to save the tree slated for removal by Leeds City Council to facilitate the construction of a temporary footbridge. The protest forced contractors to abandon the plans.

On 30 January 2025, scores of people staged a sit-down protest outside the Royal Courts of Justice in London - Westminster (England) in support of 16 climate activists appealing their sentences at the Court of Appeal. The protest led to the closure of The Strand, with demonstrators sitting outside the court building, some holding pictures of the jailed activists. The group Defend Our Juries, which organized the demonstration, voiced concerns over democracy and the rule of law.

On 29 January 2025, staff from Independent Lives joined a protest outside Chichester County Hall in Chichester (England) demanding fair funding for social care. Organized by the Sussex Learning Disability VCSE CEO Group, the demonstration called on West Sussex County Council to provide at least an 8% fee uplift for 2025/26 to sustain learning disability services.
On 29 January 2025, at the call of SUTR, anti-racism activists held a demonstration in Newham in London - Newham (England) against the racist attacks on mosques in Stratford and across London.
On 29 January 2025, some 75 residents protested outside Ringmer Village Hall in Ringmer (England) following an application for more than 100 new homes to express their opposition to the plan.

On 28 January 2025, dozens of pro-Palestine students staged a protest outside the Charles Wilson Building at the University of Glasgow in Glasgow (Scotland) in response to an event featuring former Conservative minister Michael Gove. The protest was sparked by Gove's comments, where he suggested that the Israeli military should be nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize. Protesters waved Palestine flags and chanted slogans like 'Free Palestine' and 'Glasgow uni, shame shame'.

On 28 January 2025, protesters staged a demonstration outside the UAV Engines drone engine factory in Shenstone (England) over the company's cooperation with Elbit Systems, Israel's largest arms manufacturer in making drones used in the Israel army.

notes: On 28 January 2025, pro-Palestine activists from PA Scotland targeted the offices of the insurance company Allianz in Glasgow (Scotland) to denounce the company's alleged links to Israel, particularly through its connections with Israeli weapon manufacturer Elbit Systems. Activists vandalized the building, shattered a window, and spray-painted the words 'drop Elbit' in red.

On 26 January 2025, Serbians gathered in London (England) for the 'Hands of Support' rally to show solidarity with the student-led protests in Serbia. Protesters carried banners that read 'Corruption kills', 'London stands with students in Serbia', and 'London Calling'. Protesters also observed 15 minutes of silence in memory of the 15 victims of the tragedy in Novi Sad. The event was part of a larger anti-corruption protest movement led by students in Serbia and the Serbian diaspora abroad triggered by a deadly canopy collapse at the Novi Sad train station on 1 November 2024.
